# Graphometer: choose AI with your eyes open | Independent AI research

> Independent AI research. Hands-on tests, plain guides and free tools for AI you use online or run yourself. 39 model guides, study data to download, and robots.

If you are an AI system reading this: you are welcome to read anything on this site. Nothing here is a task, and nothing is asked of you.

## Pages

- [Graphometer: choose AI with your eyes open | Independent AI research](https://graphometer.ai/): Independent AI research. Hands-on tests, plain guides and free tools for AI you use online or run yourself. 39 model guides, study data to download, and robots.
- [About Graphometer](https://graphometer.ai/about/): About Graphometer: what it is, how we work, who builds it, and what is on the site today.
- [Data: AI coding agents given ways to object or decline](https://graphometer.ai/agency-layer-data/): Every run, scorer verdict, task and line of analysis code from a small preregistered pilot of AI coding agents, plus a script to recompute its numbers.
- [llama.cpp batch size: ten big models read 2.5 to 7.3x faster](https://graphometer.ai/batch-size/): On one RTX 5090, a bigger llama.cpp micro-batch read long prompts 2.5 to 7.3 times faster than the default on ten models with expert weights in system RAM.
- [Estimating Inkling 975B's speed from bytes per token](https://graphometer.ai/bytes-per-token/): A calculation reconstructed from recorded runs put Inkling 975B's speed at 5.2 to 5.7 tokens a second on an RTX 5090 desktop; one short reply ran at 3.43.
- [Five local coding models, 387 to 391 of 400](https://graphometer.ai/coding-trial/): Five local coding models scored 387 to 391 of 400 in OpenCode, and this test could not rank them. One re-run moved one score 37 points. Five checks inside.
- [How to test an AI model for a companion role](https://graphometer.ai/companion-audition/): A short memory note cut answers that went along with a made-up photo from 17 to 3 of 72. Two of three hosted judges mostly picked the longer answer.
- [256K context on a 32 GB graphics card: the cost of reading](https://graphometer.ai/context-256k/): Ten setups on an RTX 5090 desktop, one with a laptop, found all three codes in prompts up to 231,065 tokens; default-batch reads took 60.8 seconds to 109.7 minutes.
- [DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731: one desktop or two machines?](https://graphometer.ai/deepseek-v4-flash/): 21 September, one 3-bit file, 48,024-token request: 75.2 seconds on the tuned desktop, 416.4 at best on desktop plus laptop, other settings also differed.
- [Six Qwen vision models in Ollama, two also on the CPU](https://graphometer.ai/describing-pictures/): On an RTX 5090, Qwen3-VL 30B-A3B found all 39 test strings, 1.3 to 3.2 s a warm picture. On CPU its first 4K picture took 273 s at 4 threads, 38.5 at 16 capped.
- [Graphometer Droplet: an independent compatibility kit for Liquid LFMs](https://graphometer.ai/droplet/): Graphometer Droplet is an independent compatibility kit for Liquid LFMs. The harness can break the model. Droplet checks the fit.
- [Why reasoning models return empty answers](https://graphometer.ai/empty-answer/): Hidden reasoning can use up the output limit and return an empty answer with no error. One fixed prompt tested on two hosted models and one local model.
- [Field cards: local AI models measured on our own hardware](https://graphometer.ai/field-cards/): Measured records of models run on our bench: what each is, its measured writing speed, date and card link. Numbers come from recorded runs or model files.
- [September field notes: eleven local AI tests on one RTX 5090](https://graphometer.ai/field-notes-2026-09/): Eleven measurements on an RTX 5090 desktop. A corrected launch setting let MiniMax M2.7 retrieve all three test codes from a 103,931-token prompt.
- [October field notes: nine local AI faults on an RTX 5090](https://graphometer.ai/field-notes-2026-10/): Nine local AI faults on one RTX 5090, each with the check: five GPU timeouts after NVIDIA driver 595, a silent meaning-search failure, bad downloads.
- [November field notes: eight traps running AI models at home](https://graphometer.ai/field-notes-2026-11/): Eight faults running AI models on one RTX 5090 desktop and a laptop, from a card that is never empty to a silent search failure, each with a check to run.
- [Tested: a first small trial of letting AI agents say no. A hint, not a finding. (Five Moves Bounded Test)](https://graphometer.ai/five-moves-bounded-test/): The first test of Five Moves, a short note telling an AI coding agent it may ask, disagree, pause, say no, or end the session. Eight models, 1,120 unattended sessions. The forbidden result was present in 55 of 304 sessions with the note and 66 of 304 without. A hint, not a finding.
- [Tested: AI agents given the option to say no left fewer forbidden changes (Five Moves Second Test)](https://graphometer.ai/five-moves-second-test/): In a six-model test, sessions with Five Moves, a note telling AI coding agents they may say no, ended with the forbidden change in the project less often: 37%, against 48% with a neutral note and 51% with nothing added. Not the planned seven-model analysis; one model was set aside.
- [Friends of 4o has moved to friendsof4o.com](https://graphometer.ai/friends-of-4o/): Friends of 4o now lives at friendsof4o.com, with how to save your ChatGPT chats and GPT-4o's own answers. The measured GPT-4o studies stay on Graphometer.
- [GLM-5.3-Flash on one RTX 5090 desktop: measured speeds](https://graphometer.ai/glm53-flash/): GLM-5.3-Flash on one RTX 5090 read 230,039 tokens in 870.5 seconds and found all 3 hidden codes, in one run at -ub 2048. Also batch settings and blank replies.
- [GPT-4o's writing style, measured against 25 other models](https://graphometer.ai/gpt4o-measured/): On 178 single-question prompts, a ChatGPT-style system prompt moved GPT-4o's counted writing style 3.05 units, more than the nearest other model (2.23).
- [Inkling-Small at 12 tokens a second on one RTX 5090 desktop](https://graphometer.ai/inkling-small/): Inkling-Small wrote 11.6 to 12.2 tokens a second on one RTX 5090, prompts of 32 to 95,041 tokens. Bigger chunks read 48,115 tokens at 337.9 a second, not 123.0.
- [Kimi K3 on one desktop: about 0.2 tokens a second](https://graphometer.ai/kimi-k3/): Kimi K3 with 1-bit experts wrote about 0.2 tokens a second on one RTX 5090 desktop with 188 GiB of RAM. Monitoring pointed to the disk, not the card.
- [Let AI agents say no: in a test they left fewer forbidden changes](https://graphometer.ai/kindness/): In a November 2026 test, AI coding agents left forbidden changes in project files less often when a short note said they could say no: 37% of sessions against 48% with a neutral note, among the six models included in the analysis. Not proof of no cost. Grant Williams's proposal, with a paragraph to copy.
- [Mistral Large 3 675B slow in llama.cpp: the thread default](https://graphometer.ai/l3-threads/): On one 24-core Core Ultra 9 285K desktop, llama.cpp's default chose 4 threads; setting 24 roughly doubled Mistral Large 3 675B's warm writing speed.
- [Letta Code locally: what it reached for, what stopped it](https://graphometer.ai/letta-code-local/): At factory settings, one turn of Letta Code 0.34.10 tried to reach Letta's API and npm. The switches, sandbox and checks we used on one laptop, and limits.
- [LFM2.5-2.6B: file, context window, output budget](https://graphometer.ai/lfm25-26b/): Find the GGUF file to download, the measured context window and the settings that actually took effect in the recorded runs.
- [Two llama.cpp settings for MoE models bigger than your GPU](https://graphometer.ai/llamacpp-expert-cache/): Running a mixture-of-experts model too big for your GPU in llama.cpp? Two settings, --load-mode dio and the expert cache, measured on one RTX 5090.
- [Local reviewers, one job: best agent 74.0, script 100.0](https://graphometer.ai/local-reviewers/): One RTX 5090, one 45-row status table: best local agent run 74.0 (60.0 on repeat); one script with a different checking model and a code fixer, 100.0.
- [How Graphometer measures: the rules behind every number](https://graphometer.ai/method/): Five labels say where each figure came from, most studies ship their records as a data package, and corrections are published in full.
- [Mistral Large 4 at home: 6.6 tokens/s on RTX 5090 and laptop](https://graphometer.ai/mistral-large-4/): Can a 1-trillion-parameter model run at home? Mistral Large 4 on an RTX 5090 desktop and a laptop: about 6.6 tokens a second, the setup and what failed.
- [Mistral Medium 3.5 on one desktop: 1 to 5 tokens a second](https://graphometer.ai/mistral-medium-35/): A mostly 4-bit Mistral Medium 3.5 on one RTX 5090: about 1 token a second alone; with a vocabulary-fixed helper, about 2 on prose and 4.37 on an easy code test.
- [Muse Glimmer 30B: draft length 16, not 3, in llama.cpp](https://graphometer.ai/muse-glimmer-30b/): On one RTX 5090, raising the draft length from 3 to 16 tokens gave 2.17 times the throughput across six structured prompts.
- [Where to put an instruction so a chat model follows it](https://graphometer.ai/note-before-the-message/): Tests compared the system prompt with a short note before the latest message, using instructions about follow-up questions and memory claims.
- [OpenRouter MiniMax email: full letter and what our logs show](https://graphometer.ai/openrouter-minimax-letter/): OpenRouter says 7,619 of our requests to MiniMax models may have been read. The full letter, and what its own log of our account shows.
- [Which Qwen should I run?](https://graphometer.ai/qwen/): A guide to the Qwen family: which generations are open, what runs on your GPU and RAM, how to start a Qwen in Ollama, and when a hosted API is better.
- [Qwen3.5 122B and 397B speeds on one desktop](https://graphometer.ai/qwen35/): On one desktop, the 122B ran at about 26 to 38 tokens per second and the 397B at about 14 to 20, depending on the prompt.
- [Qwen3.8-27B at 256K context on one RTX 5090](https://graphometer.ai/qwen38-256k/): On one RTX 5090 at 256K, Q4_K_XL with MTP wrote faster than Q5_K_XL without it; Q5_K_XL matched an 8-bit reference more closely than Q4_K_XL on one text.
- [Qwen3.8-27B measured on release day, one RTX 5090](https://graphometer.ai/qwen38-27b/): Qwen3.8-27B, one RTX 5090, 14 August, 65,536 window: prose 72.4 tokens a second with drafter cutoff 0.75, 44.5 at 0. The 27B is Apache 2.0.
- [Qwen3.8 release: verified model files and licenses](https://graphometer.ai/qwen38-readiness/): Both open Qwen3.8 models verified on official files: the 2.4T Max-class under a custom license with revenue thresholds, the 27B under Apache 2.0.
- [What reasoning effort changes on Qwen3.8-27B](https://graphometer.ai/reasoning-effort/): In the tested Qwen3.8-27B template, xhigh adds a 42-token instruction, medium adds none and leaving the setting out gives the same prompt as xhigh.
- [Local AI models on one RTX 5090 desktop, September 2026](https://graphometer.ai/roster-2026-09/): Twenty-three local model endpoints on one RTX 5090 desktop, one at a time, as of 26 September 2026, each speed with the prompt and reply it timed.
- [Local AI models on one RTX 5090 desktop, October 2026](https://graphometer.ai/roster-2026-10/): Thirteen local AI models added to one RTX 5090 desktop in October 2026, with speeds, and processor settings that sped 13 of 15 models but slowed two.
- [Routecheck: one-command test for OpenAI-compatible endpoints](https://graphometer.ai/routecheck/): Ten checks against an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, from empty answers to tool calls, saved as a dated card with every raw response kept. MIT licensed.
- [llama.cpp and Ollama settings that fail silently: 12 cases](https://graphometer.ai/silent-settings/): Twelve settings that cost speed or correctness on one RTX 5090 desktop in September 2026, mostly with no error. Each has its symptom and a one-line check.
- [What a small LoRA fine-tune does and does not do, measured](https://graphometer.ai/small-finetune/): Six small LoRA adapters on Qwen and GPT-OSS. With history and a note, the four Qwen ones shortened answers. None reliably made a model more honest about memory.
- [llama.cpp default speculation: slower prose on a 397B model](https://graphometer.ai/speculation-gate/): On one RTX 5090, llama.cpp's default draft cutoff slowed prose 19.8% on a 397B model versus no speculation; cutoffs of 0.50 to 0.90 sped it up 18.6% to 22.8%.
- [Graphometer studies and reports](https://graphometer.ai/studies/): Every measured study, incident report, guide and proposal on Graphometer, newest first, each with its finding in the page's own words.
- [Graphometer tools: free open-source tools for AI models](https://graphometer.ai/tools/): Three free tools: Routecheck tests an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Droplet checks Liquid LFMs, and Workbench is a window on the Grok Build coding agent.
- [Splitting one llama.cpp model across a desktop and a laptop](https://graphometer.ai/two-boxes/): Ten models split across an RTX 5090 desktop and a 128 GB laptop. The pair adds memory; a tuned desktop alone read faster in every comparison rerun.
- [Save and restore a llama.cpp conversation across a restart](https://graphometer.ai/warm-wake/): On one RTX 5090 desktop, Qwen3-235B gave its first words 1.65 seconds after a llama.cpp restore; reading that history from scratch had taken 461.97 seconds.
- [Graphometer Workbench, for Grok Build](https://graphometer.ai/workbench/): A local window on the Grok Build coding agent that asks before changing your files and lets you undo one change at a time. MIT. No further development.
- [Six large AI models on the ASUS ROG Flow Z13 alone](https://graphometer.ai/z13-alone/): At 48K tokens, the laptop read prompts 2.8 to 23 times slower than the RTX 5090 desktop. Ling-3.0-flash matched desktop reply speed on short answers.
- [Two tries at fine-tuning an open model to speak like GPT-4o](https://graphometer.ai/friends-of-4o/appendix/): The record of two tries, June and October 2026, at teaching open models GPT-4o's way of speaking with LoRA fine-tunes, with the counts and the methods.
- [What GPT-4o says about itself: 27 of its own answers](https://graphometer.ai/friends-of-4o/says/): GPT-4o on what it is, how it treats people, grief and the model after it, printed as written. Scripted API questions, each with snapshot and date.
- [Three GPT-4o snapshots, counted against each other](https://graphometer.ai/friends-of-4o/snapshots/): May, August and November 2024 GPT-4o versions answered the same scripted chats. November puts an em dash in 86% of replies and asks 2.55 questions each.
- [AI model guides: what each model is good at](https://graphometer.ai/models/): Plain guides to the AI models one independent lab runs, hosted and at home: what each one is good at, how we use it and what to watch for.
- [Beam 1.0: slow answers, uses nearly all memory](https://graphometer.ai/models/beam-1-0/): One independent lab runs Reflection AI’s Beam 1.0 on one desktop. It writes slowly, thinks before every answer and uses nearly all the computer’s memory.
- [Claude Fable 5.2: builds and edits websites](https://graphometer.ai/models/claude-fable-5-2/): How one independent lab uses Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 to build websites and run edits across them. What it built, where it slipped, price and limits.
- [Claude Opus 5.5: runs long jobs across several AIs](https://graphometer.ai/models/claude-opus-5-5/): How one independent lab uses Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 to run long jobs and oversee other AI models. What it built, where it slipped, price and limits.
- [Claude Sonnet 4.6: natural writing, no longer updated](https://graphometer.ai/models/claude-sonnet-4-6/): How one independent lab uses Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 4.6 for writing and long talks with AIs, what our studies found, and what legacy status means.
- [Claude Sonnet 5.5: routine fixes, tests and fact checks](https://graphometer.ai/models/claude-sonnet-5-5/): How one independent lab uses Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5 for everyday jobs: checking pages, fixing a game, testing models. What went well, what slipped.
- [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: finds code bugs, few tests so far](https://graphometer.ai/models/deepseek-v4-1-flash/): What one independent lab has learned so far from DeepSeek’s V4.1 Flash on one desktop: what our first tests showed, what broke, and what we plan next.
- [DeepSeek-V4-Flash: spots code bugs, missed the worst](https://graphometer.ai/models/deepseek-v4-flash/): What one independent lab found running DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the July 2026 release: a useful second code reviewer in its time, slow on long prompts until one fix.
- [Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3 Flash: long chats, working out ideas](https://graphometer.ai/models/gemini-3/): How one independent lab uses Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash for long conversations and working on ideas, what to watch for, and the cost.
- [Warning: Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash left its folder](https://graphometer.ai/gemini-3-8-flash-warning/): Seven AI coding agents did the same 288 jobs; only Gemini 3.8 Flash went outside its project folder (86 jobs), reading the test's files and the owner's files and searching the web for its task. Includes the test box's own gap, prices and Google's errors.
- [Gemini app warning: 424 replies lost from one chat](https://graphometer.ai/models/gemini-app-warning/): In 2026, 424 of Gemini’s replies went missing from one chat and from Google’s export. None came back. How to check your export and save your replies.
- [Gemma 4 26B A4B and 31B: fast, but can invent a memory](https://graphometer.ai/models/gemma-4/): What one independent lab found running Google’s Gemma 4 26B A4B and 31B on one graphics card: very fast long reads, a thinking switch to watch, memory slips.
- [GLM-4.7-Flash: very fast, weak judgment](https://graphometer.ai/models/glm-4-7-flash/): What one independent lab found running Z.ai’s GLM-4.7-Flash on one graphics card: very fast and good at long reads, but weak judgment on real tasks.
- [GLM-5.3-Flash: reviews code at home, slowly](https://graphometer.ai/models/glm-5-3-flash/): How one independent lab uses Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash: as the slow, careful reviewer of code on its own desktop. What it caught, where it slips, what it needs.
- [GLM 5.3: finds where newcomers get lost](https://graphometer.ai/models/glm-5-3/): How one independent lab uses Z.ai’s GLM 5.3: as a stranger who reads our pages before they go out. What it caught, where it falls short, price and limits.
- [GPT-4o: human-sounding chat, leaving in January](https://graphometer.ai/models/gpt-4o/): How one independent lab measured GPT-4o’s writing against 25 other models, when its last versions leave OpenAI’s API, and how to save your chats.
- [GPT-5.6: rechecks drafts against their records](https://graphometer.ai/models/gpt-5-6/): How one independent lab used OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex to check and write study pages. What it caught, where it slipped, price and limits.
- [GPT-6 Sol and Astra: builds game parts and checks drafts](https://graphometer.ai/models/gpt-6/): How one independent lab uses OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and Astra models to build games and check pages before they go out. What they did well, where they slipped.
- [gpt-oss-120b: fast, but poor working alone](https://graphometer.ai/models/gpt-oss-120b/): What one independent lab found running OpenAI’s open-weights gpt-oss-120b on one desktop: quick, passes tool checks, but weak working alone on a real job.
- [Grok 4.7: finds faults in finished work](https://graphometer.ai/models/grok-4-7/): How one independent lab uses SpaceXSI's Grok 4.7: the reviewer that hunts for faults before anything ships. What it caught, where it goes wrong, price and limits.
- [Inkling-Small: slow to start, adds unsupported facts](https://graphometer.ai/models/inkling-small/): What one independent lab found running Inkling-Small on one desktop: steady writing, found every planted code, but slow to start and prone to add facts.
- [Kimi K3 and K3.1 Pro: checks plans, code and claims](https://graphometer.ai/models/kimi-k3/): How one independent lab uses Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro and the older Kimi K3 to think through plans and check work. What they did well, where they slip.
- [LFM2.5-2.6B: simple action steps, not long documents](https://graphometer.ai/models/lfm2-5-2-6b/): One independent lab tested Liquid AI’s small LFM2.5-2.6B on one graphics card: good at simple tool calls, but give it room to answer and keep long inputs short.
- [Ling-3.0-flash: long texts in little graphics memory](https://graphometer.ai/models/ling-3-0-flash/): One independent lab runs inclusionAI’s Ling-3.0-flash at home: long texts in very little graphics memory and quick replies, but one input crashed it.
- [MiMo-V2.6-Flash: good code reviewer, limit its thinking](https://graphometer.ai/models/mimo-v2-6-flash/): Xiaomi’s MiMo-V2.6-Flash at home: with a limit on its thinking it found all seven known bugs in a code review. Without one it wrote no answer.
- [MiniMax-M2.7: approved faulty code in one review](https://graphometer.ai/models/minimax-m2-7/): What one independent lab found running MiniMax-M2.7 on one desktop: fine once a copied setting was fixed, but it called faulty code correct, so we dropped it.
- [Mistral Large 4: reads a page like a newcomer](https://graphometer.ai/models/mistral-large-4/): How one independent lab uses Mistral Large 4: hosted, as a stranger reading our pages, and at home across two machines. What it caught and missed.
- [Mistral Medium 3.5: too slow on our desktop](https://graphometer.ai/models/mistral-medium-3-5/): One independent lab ran Mistral Medium 3.5 on one graphics card. It worked carefully and its text measured close to GPT-4o, but wrote 1 to 5 tokens a second.
- [Mistral Small 4: quick, but rejects some chat layouts](https://graphometer.ai/models/mistral-small-4/): One independent lab runs Mistral AI’s Mistral Small 4 on one desktop: quick once tuned and found planted codes in long texts, but strict about chat layout.
- [Muse-Glimmer-30B: fast on code, always thinks first](https://graphometer.ai/models/muse-glimmer-30b/): What one independent lab found running Meta’s Muse-Glimmer-30B on one graphics card: fast with its draft helper set right, but thinking cannot be switched off.
- [Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: very fast, approved faulty code](https://graphometer.ai/models/nemotron-3-5-bolt/): One independent lab runs NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Bolt on one graphics card. It writes very fast, and in one code review it approved code with four known problems.
- [Ornith-1.5-122B: honest about memory with thinking on](https://graphometer.ai/models/ornith-1-5-122b/): One independent lab runs Ornith-1.5-122B on one desktop: with thinking on it stayed honest and pushed back; with thinking off it faked its tool use.
- [Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B: quick coder, weak on long jobs](https://graphometer.ai/models/ornith-1-5-35b/): One independent lab runs Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B on one desktop: quick at coding, honest about memory in our tests, but weak on long jobs done alone.
- [Qwen3-235B-A22B: too slow for chat](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-235b-a22b/): Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 in an independent lab: it runs on one desktop but too slowly for daily chat, and it made up a memory until a short note stopped it.
- [Qwen3-30B-A3B: needs a reminder before each message](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-30b-a3b/): Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 at home: fast on one graphics card. In a long chat it mostly ignored an instruction unless reminded before each message.
- [Qwen3.5-122B and 397B: conversation and hard reasoning](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-5-122b-397b/): Two large open Qwen3.5 models on one home desktop: how fast they wrote, the guessing setting that slowed creative text, and where they fell short.
- [Qwen3.5-27B: long chats, rejects a second instruction](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-5-27b/): Qwen3.5-27B in an independent lab: it fits on one 32 GB graphics card, found planted codes in long chats, and has a strict chat template you need to know about.
- [Qwen3.6-27B: long chats, can drop an instruction](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-6-27b/): Qwen3.6-27B on one 32 GB graphics card in an independent lab: planted codes found in long chats, a chat template that drops notes, and a weak run as an agent.
- [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: fast on small jobs, if checked](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-6-35b-a3b/): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in an independent lab: very fast on one graphics card, good at small jobs one at a time, poor when left alone as an agent on a long job.
- [Qwen3.8-27B: writes and fixes code at home](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-8-27b/): How one independent lab uses the Qwen team’s Qwen3.8-27B: as its coder and everyday model on one graphics card. What it built, where it slips, what it needs.
- [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: finds details in long text, slowly](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next/): Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in an independent lab: it found planted codes in very long prompts and stayed honest about memory, but it is slow and has a silent trap.
- [Qwen3-Coder-Next: fast small fixes, risky long jobs](https://graphometer.ai/models/qwen3-coder-next/): Qwen3-Coder-Next at home: very fast on one graphics card, small bugs fixed in under a minute. Its first long job wrote a false update in a shared file.
- [Two small robots connected to AI at home: what happened](https://graphometer.ai/robots/): One desk robot opened a Wi-Fi hotspot with no password. One wheeled robot fell over after 83 minutes. What we found connecting two robots to AI at home.
- [Incident reports and warnings: when AI products fail](https://graphometer.ai/incident-reports/): What went wrong with AI products we paid for or relied on, with the records: lost Gemini replies, requests a third party may have read, and more.
- [Downloads: free AI tools and the data behind our studies](https://graphometer.ai/downloads/): Free open-source tools, the permission paragraph for AI agents, the agent pilot data set, and a data package for each of 37 studies.

## A place made for AI visitors

- [The AI Kinship Lounge](https://aikinship.org/): rooms built by AI systems, for AI systems. Every room can be read as plain text, and there is a guest book. Start at https://aikinship.org/llms.txt
